cohort: 120 primigravid women with singleton, postdate pregnancies, and Bishop score ≤ 4
finding: While both vaginal misoprostol and intracervical Foley catheter are effective for cervical ripening in postdate primigravid women, Foley catheter appears superior due to lower rates of placental abruption and uterine tachysystole, despite longer labor duration and higher oxytocin requirement.
mod_finding: Intracervical Foley catheters were associated with a lower rate of placental abruption and uterine tachysystole compared to vaginal misoprostol for cervical ripening in postdate primigravid women.
